# Review — PAN-4945
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — revoking an OAuth access token in Settings or with `pan token revoke` is silently undone after the 7-day prune (FR-6 / AC-5)

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4945-review-1171fef8
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4945/.pan/review/agent-pan-4945-review-1171fef8/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-4945 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4945
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/4979
- HEAD reviewed: 1171fef8aa753efb6767a90c1f9229088e215fe6
- Base: 907e9dea39d (merge-base with origin/main); prior cycle: none
- Spec: `.pan/drafts/PAN-4945.md` (D-1..D-15, FR-1..FR-10, NFR-1..NFR-9, AC-1..AC-12)

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness/security] A Settings or `pan token revoke` revocation of an OAuth access token is undone by the 7-day prune — `src/lib/access-tokens.ts:518`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: specification defect, in_pr_scope. The code follows two PRD clauses that contradict each other:
  - FR-1: "`pruneEndedAccessTokens` also removes OAuth records more than `olderThanMs` after their `revokedAt` or `expiresAt`."
  - D-8.6: "A record that no longer exists, because it expired and was pruned, is not a revocation."
  Once a revoked-but-unexpired record can be pruned, "missing" no longer means "expired".
- Trigger and changed-code connection: the operator revokes the sign-in's current access token under Settings → Access Tokens (or `pan token revoke`). `pruneEndedAccessTokens` (`access-tokens.ts:512-524`) computes `ended = Math.min(revokedAt, expiresAt)` for OAuth records, so the primary dashboard's 10-minute sweep (`agent-token-sweep.ts:94`, `AGENT_TOKEN_PRUNE_AFTER_MS = 7 days` at line 28) deletes the record 7 days after revocation. On the next refresh, `rotate` (`oauth-service.ts:480-484`) finds no record, treats it as pruned-by-expiry, and mints a new access token.
- Expected / observed / impact: expected (FR-6, AC-5, D-9, and `configuration/mcp.mdx` "Revoking"): the family ends at its next refresh. Observed: if that refresh comes more than 7 days after the revocation, the sign-in continues with a fresh 30-day token and no operator involvement. The trigger is realistic: SDK clients refresh only on a 401 or at expiry, so an idle connector passing the 7-day mark is the normal case. With PAN-4946 not shipped, Settings → Access Tokens is the only dashboard-GUI path to revoke an OAuth token in this slice. `pan mcp oauth revoke` and `DELETE /api/mcp-oauth/sign-ins/:familyId` are unaffected (they mark the family revoked).
- Evidence: runtime probe against this HEAD's source (`npx tsx`, scratchpad script, isolated temporary `OVERDECK_HOME`, service built with an injected clock): register → authorize → approve `operate` → exchange (`exchange ok true`) → `revokeAccessToken(family.accessTokenId)` → clock +8 days → `pruneEndedAccessTokens(7 days, now)` (`pruned 1`) → `refresh` → `true NEW ACCESS TOKEN MINTED`. The existing test "still refreshes when the current access record was pruned from the registry" (`tests/unit/lib/mcp/oauth-service.test.ts:313`) already shows the missing-record path succeeds.
- Fix: correct FR-1 so OAuth records are pruned by `expiresAt` only; then a missing record always means expired and D-8.6 holds. Code: `access-tokens.ts:518` `Math.min(revoked, Date.parse(record.expiresAt!))` → `Date.parse(record.expiresAt!)`; update that function's doc comment, the module-header sentence, and `docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md` ("OAuth records are removed 7 days after they expire"). Add a regression test shaped like the probe: revoke the current access token → `pruneEndedAccessTokens(7d, now + 8d)` → refresh answers `invalid_grant` and the family has `revokedAt`. Adjust `access-tokens-oauth.test.ts` prune expectations accordingly. (Making `rotate` treat a missing record as revoked is weaker: the family does not store its current token's expiry, so it cannot tell the two cases apart.)

## Non-blocking Findings

### [security] Unauthenticated OAuth routes read the whole body before any size check — `src/dashboard/server/routes/mcp-oauth.ts:95`
- Severity: ~
- Classification / scope: validation gap; in_pr_scope (new routes), but the pattern is pre-existing across the server (no `maxBodySize` anywhere in `src/dashboard/server`).
- Trigger: `POST /oauth/mcp/register`, `/oauth/mcp/token` (line 134) and `/oauth/mcp/revoke` (line 147) are outside the gate and reachable by any LAN peer (H-1). `yield* request.text` buffers the full body; the 16 KiB check on register runs after the read, and token/revoke have no limit.
- Impact: a LAN peer can make the dashboard buffer an arbitrarily large body without a credential. Bounded by the accepted LAN threat model today; it matters more once W-FUN1 (PAN-4947) opens Funnel.
- Evidence: static read; `grep maxBodySize` finds nothing in the server.
- Fix (suggested, before or with W-FUN1): read with a byte cap (stream or `Content-Length` precheck) on these three routes.

### [security] A LAN peer can evict a real pending approval by flooding authorize — `src/lib/mcp/oauth-service.ts:333`
- Severity: ?
- Classification: hypothesis / accepted hazard (PRD H-1). The 21st pending approval drops the oldest one, so 20 junk authorize requests push out a legitimate sign-in in progress. No data exposure; the user restarts the sign-in. Rate limits arrive only for Funnel in W-FUN1. Worth a per-source cap if LAN abuse is ever a concern.

### [spec] OAuth access tokens also authenticate `/api/*` and `/ws/*`, not only `/mcp`
- Severity: ?
- Classification: specification note, not an implementation defect. D-7.5 makes the access token an ordinary `kind: 'token'` record, so the remote gate admits it on any route its scopes satisfy (there is no RFC 8707 audience binding; `resource` is ignored per D-5). The scope ceiling (NFR-2) bounds the reach. If the epic intends `/mcp`-only tokens, that is a spec change for a later item.

### [correctness] `DELETE /api/mcp-oauth/sign-ins/:familyId` on a refresh-expired, unrevoked family revokes it but answers 404 — `src/lib/mcp/oauth-service.ts:202`
- Severity: ~ (cosmetic)
- `endFamily` writes `revokedAt` and revokes the tokens, then returns `refreshExpiresAt > at`, so the route says "no active sign-in". Consistent with `listSignIns`, which hides such families; no user harm.

### [correctness] `POST /oauth/mcp/revoke` with an access token already revoked in Settings does not end the family — `src/lib/mcp/oauth-service.ts:525`
- Severity: ? 
- `readActiveAccessTokenRecord` returns null for a revoked record, so no family is found. The family still ends at its next refresh (D-8.6, tested), so the outcome only arrives later. Matches D-9 as written.

### [spec] Code-exchange check order differs from D-7's numbering — `src/lib/mcp/oauth-service.ts:425`
- Not a defect. The implementation checks `used` before expiry, so a reused code inside the 10-minute retention window still revokes its family. This is what D-6's "kept that long only to detect reuse" intends; the code comments it. D-7 steps 1-2 could be reworded in the PRD.

### [docs] `.overdeck/context/codebase/concerns.md:684` leaves two stacked `last-verified` comments
- Cosmetic: the new line was added above the old ones instead of replacing them.

### [ux] Settings → Access Tokens shows an expired OAuth token as active until it is pruned
- Severity: ?
- `toPublic` keeps `expiresAt`, and `GET /api/access-tokens` lists every record, but the Settings list has no expiry notion, so an expired, unrevoked OAuth token looks active for up to 7 days. Consistent with the non-goal of not touching `routes/access-tokens.ts`; a natural fit for PAN-4946.

### Dimensions
- **Correctness:** traced every entry point (routes → service → store/registry) including concurrency (serialized refresh queue, code reuse during mint), clock use (service `now` vs registry `Date.now`), prune interplay, and the SDK client path end to end. One blocker (prune vs D-8.6 revocation detection); the rest are advisories.
- **Security:** trust boundary is the unauthenticated `/.well-known/*` and `/oauth/mcp/*` surface. Redirects only to registered URIs (step 1 error page otherwise); PKCE S256 mandatory with constant-time compare; refresh tokens stored as SHA-256 only; no tokens in logs (`logFailure` prints store/registry error messages, which name paths, not tokens); HTML escaped, nonce CSP, no framing, no referrer; issuer chosen from the trusted-origin allowlist so Host/X-Forwarded-Host spoofing cannot inject URLs; no CORS headers; Funnel still 404 (gate untouched, tested). Operator routes are root-only after the gate. Advisories above.
- **Performance:** all state bounded (50 clients, 20 pending approvals, codes tied to operator decisions, 20 prior hashes per family); store reads are small JSON files; no sync I/O (NFR-4). Body-size advisory above.
- **Requirements/UX:** see the matrix. CLI messages match D-13; non-goals respected (no UI, no gate/route-scopes change, no CORS, no expiry event, no custom schemes/secrets/other grants, no OIDC, no change to `routes/access-tokens.ts` or `cli/commands/token.ts`, no `cli/mcp.mdx`).
